input = use to build and tune the tool; test = keep aside until the tool is finished, then score once. Test: Tehri Garhwal, the 10 Spring Atlas profile springs, their 30 m groups, and springs within 2 km of these.

Blank for records with no other record within 30 m. Otherwise: same spring, different springs, partly the same spring, or needs review (for the whole 30 m group).

For records within 30 m of another: the group, which records are the same spring, which are separate springs and why, and which still need a person's decision. Coloured in the workbook; every pair is on the Duplicate pairs sheet.

Only where DEM and source elevation differ by more than 150 m: which is probably wrong. Copied coordinate (another record at the same point fits the DEM), coordinate a little off (the source elevation is found within 300 m), coordinate off by the stated distance, or no point within 2 km has the source elevation.

Highest minus lowest elevation within 1 km.

Surface area draining to the spring cell (multiple-flow-direction routing on the filled DEM). The topographic catchment above the spring; not the recharge area, which follows the rocks.
Largest drainage area within about 30 m (allows for GPS error). Much larger than drainage_area_ha means a hollow or stream line is right next to the point.
Topographic wetness index ln(a / tan slope). Higher = wetter, more convergent spot. Hillslopes ~4-8, hollows and valley floors ~8-14.
